Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alaska's adoption of NAIC Model 582 is read as the representative text (Sections 5 policy scope, 6 basic illustration content, 7 annual report and in-force illustration, 10 record retention, 11 annual illustration actuary certification), cross-read each review cycle against the Alabama, Arizona and California adoptions and ASOP No. 24

In-scope processes.value: Group Life illustration production, producer delivery and applicant signature at point of sale; in-force illustration on request; annual policy owner report; illustration actuary annual certification; illustration software change control

In-scope systems.value: Illustration engine and certificate master in the policy administration system, with signed illustrations imaged into the document management repository and the procedure itself versioned in the GRC platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Life Insurance Illustration Compliance Procedure (Group Life) — illustrated vs non-illustrated designation, basic illustration content and labelling, guaranteed / midpoint / illustrated-scale columns, prohibited practices, signature and delivery, annual report, certification calendar

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with concurring sign-off from the illustration actuary and Regulatory Counsel; reviewed every year before the certification cycle and on any state adoption amendment or NAIC Model 582 revision

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual procedure review closes before the illustration actuary certification is presented to the board; the certification and the officer certification are filed with each domiciliary and licensed state on that state's annual-statement timetable (March 1 in the states that tie it to the annual statement)

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform recurring tasks: procedure review opens 1 October, redline due 15 November, approval due 31 December, certification package due 15 February ahead of the 1 March filings

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Procedure versions, approval records and the state requirements matrix retained 7 years; signed basic illustrations retained per Model 582 Section 10 — 3 years after the certificate is no longer in force

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any illustration produced outside the procedure — missing signature, non-conforming scale, prohibited wording — is logged as a market conduct exception with root cause, affected certificate numbers and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every procedure gap and every illustration-practice exception before the annual review is declared complete

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The 45 jurisdiction rows of the Model 582 requirements matrix plus every Group Life illustration produced in the review year, per the illustration engine output log

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every one of the 45 jurisdictions must map to a live procedure section with a current citation; any state requirement with no procedure step, or any procedure step citing a superseded adoption, is a fail; more than 2 fails halts publication of the procedure

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is an annual review; the test runs once a year immediately after approval, plus an out-of-cycle test whenever a state amends its Model 582 adoption mid-year

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Auditor must not have drafted or edited any section of the illustration procedure under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual illustration-procedure test workpaper (matrix extract, sampled state re-performance, sampled illustration trace, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-012-C01

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Approved procedure with version history, the 45-state requirements matrix with citations, and the illustration actuary certification, producible for a market conduct exam call letter within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance answers illustration-procedure information requests; Regulatory Counsel clears any statement about a past non-conforming illustration practice before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Fix the product and jurisdiction scope the procedure has to cover
actions: Pull from the policy administration system a list of every Group Life plan code in force or open for new sales, with writing company, NAIC co-code, states of issue and face-amount bands.

Apply the Model 582 Section 3 scope exclusions on the list: strike variable life, group and individual annuities, credit life, and certificates with a face amount of $10,000 or less, and note the striking reason on each row.
Ask the Insurance Product Manager to confirm which remaining plan codes are marketed with sales illustrations and which are sold from a rate card only.
Record the resulting in-scope plan-code list, keyed by the 45 jurisdictions in the regulation's jurisdiction scope, as Appendix A of the procedure.
checklist.done: Appendix A names every in-scope Group Life plan code by state, with a written exclusion reason on every plan code left out.

checklist.step: Build the 45-jurisdiction requirements matrix from each state's adoption of Model 582
actions: Open the regulatory library and pull each of the 45 states' life insurance illustrations regulation as adopted, starting with the representative Alaska adoption and the Alabama, Arizona and California adoptions named in the citation list.

For every state, record on its own matrix row: adoption citation, effective date, whether the state deviates from Model 582 on the annual report content, on the in-force illustration turnaround, and on the certification filing date.
Flag the states that added a delivery-receipt or a separate policy-summary requirement on top of the model — these drive extra procedure steps rather than a footnote.
Attach a dated PDF capture of each state's regulation text to its matrix row so the procedure's citations are provable at a later exam.
checklist.done: all 45 jurisdictions have a matrix row with citation, effective date, deviations and a dated text capture.

checklist.step: Have the illustration actuary settle which Group Life plans are illustrated and which are non-illustrated
actions: For each in-scope plan code, run the self-support and lapse-support tests required by Model 582 Section 5 and ASOP No. 24 on the currently payable scale in the actuarial model.

Mark plans that fail either test, or that the company chooses not to illustrate, as 'non-illustrated' and record the Section 5 identification requirement that follows (no illustration may be used for that plan).
For illustrated plans, document the disciplined current scale: the experience assumptions used, the date of the experience study behind them, and the margin against the currently payable scale.
Hand the signed designation list to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for Appendix B of the procedure and to the illustration engine owner for configuration.
checklist.done: every in-scope plan carries a dated illustrated / non-illustrated designation supported by self-support and lapse-support test output.

checklist.step: Write the basic illustration content and format section
actions: Draft the section against Model 582 Section 6: the illustration must be labelled 'Life Insurance Illustration' and carry insurer name, producer name, proposed insured or group name, plan/policy form number, generic product name, initial death benefit and dividend or premium payment option.

Specify the three required columns on the tabular detail — guaranteed, midpoint and illustrated scale — and require the numeric summary at years 5, 10, 20 and at age 70 with the guaranteed / midpoint / illustrated-scale trio on each.

Write in the mandatory narrative wording: the statement that non-guaranteed elements are not guaranteed and are based on the company's current scale which may change, and the explanation of guaranteed and non-guaranteed elements in plain language.
Require year-by-year tabular detail for the first 10 years and every fifth year to policy year 60 or age 100, and name the exact report id in the illustration engine that produces it.
Circulate the draft to the illustration engine owner to confirm each required field actually exists on the printed output before the section is signed.
checklist.done: the content section names every Model 582 Section 6 element and ties each to a printed field on the live illustration form.

checklist.step: Write the prohibited-practices section and the wording blacklist
actions: List the Model 582 Section 4 prohibitions verbatim: no illustrated scale more favourable than the disciplined current scale, no lapse-supported illustration, no illustration that is not self-supporting, no representation of the policy as anything other than life insurance.

Build the banned-wording list — 'vanish', 'vanishing premium', 'premium offset' used without the guaranteed-column caveat, 'investment', 'savings plan', 'retirement plan' — and specify the compliant alternative phrasing for each.

State the rule for producer-created material: no producer may alter, re-key or re-format an illustration, and any producer-prepared supplemental illustration must be preceded by or accompanied by the basic illustration.
Define the escalation path when a producer or a marketing piece breaches the list: immediate withdrawal, notification to the Producer Compliance Manager, and a logged market conduct exception.
checklist.done: the section carries the four statutory prohibitions, a banned-wording list with alternatives, and a named escalation path.

checklist.step: Write the annual illustration actuary certification procedure
actions: Document the annual sequence required by Model 582 Section 11: the illustration actuary certifies that the disciplined current scale conforms to ASOP No. 24, that the illustrated scales are self-supporting and not lapse-supported, and that the assumptions have been updated for the latest experience study.

Name the inputs and their owners — mortality and lapse experience study from the Valuation Actuary, expense allocation from the Controller, credited-rate history from the Chief Investment Officer's team — and set each input's due date two weeks before the certification is drafted.
Specify the officer certification that accompanies it: an authorised officer certifies the company has provided its illustration actuary with the access and information needed to certify.

Set the filing route: certification to the board of directors at its first meeting after year end, then to the insurance commissioner in each state on that state's annual-statement timetable, 1 March where the state ties the two together.
Require the certification, the supporting test output and the board minute reference to be filed together in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the certification procedure names the actuary's three assertions, the input owners with dates, the officer certification and the board plus commissioner filing route.

checklist.step: Write the annual report and in-force illustration procedure
actions: Document the Model 582 Section 7 annual report content for in-force Group Life certificates: beginning and end of period values, premiums paid in the period, interest credited, cost of insurance and expense charges deducted, and the end-of-period death benefit.

Write in the required warning: where the non-guaranteed elements at the current scale would not keep the certificate in force to the end of the next reporting period, the report must say so and tell the owner how to get an in-force illustration.

Specify the in-force illustration service level — produced on owner request within 30 days — and name the queue in the policy administration system that holds the requests and the fulfilment report that proves the turnaround.
Name the annual report production run, its calendar month, and the reconciliation the Policy Admin Ops Lead performs between the in-force certificate count and the number of reports mailed.
checklist.done: the section names the annual report data elements, the underfunding warning trigger, the 30-day in-force illustration service level and the production reconciliation.

checklist.step: Write the signature, delivery and record retention section
actions: Document the point-of-sale rule from Model 582 Section 6: the applicant and the producer both sign the basic illustration and a copy is submitted with the application; where a policy is issued other than as applied for, a revised illustration conforming to the policy as issued is signed no later than at policy delivery.
Where no illustration was used at sale, require the producer certification to that effect on the application and the delivery of the basic illustration at policy delivery.

Set the retention rule from Model 582 Section 10: keep a copy of every signed illustration for 3 years after the certificate is no longer in force, and name the retention label in the document management repository that enforces it.
Define the indexing keys the repository must hold — certificate number, group policy number, state, producer number, illustration date — so an exam sample can be pulled without a manual search.
Name the monthly control that lists applications received with no signed illustration and no producer certification, and the New Business Case Manager who clears the list.
checklist.done: the section states the signature rule, the issued-other-than-applied-for rule, the 3-year retention label and the monthly missing-illustration control.

checklist.step: Write the producer training and supervision section
actions: Specify the mandatory course — Group Life illustration standards under Model 582 — with the annual assignment date, the 80% pass mark and the 30-day completion window from assignment.

Require the roster to be built from the appointed-producer extract so every producer authorised to sell an illustrated Group Life plan in the 45 states is assigned, and reconcile the roster to that extract each quarter.

State the supervision rule: illustration output must come only from the company illustration engine or an approved vendor build; screenshots, spreadsheets and hand-typed projections are prohibited sales material.

Define the consequence ladder for non-completion or for a prohibited illustration — reminder at day 15, suspension of new business authority at day 31, referral to the Distribution Operations Manager for termination review on repeat.
Name the learning management system report id that evidences completion for an examiner.
checklist.done: the training section names the course, roster source, pass mark, completion window, consequence ladder and the evidencing report.

checklist.step: Tie each procedure rule to a configured control in the illustration engine
actions: Walk the procedure rule by rule with the illustration engine owner and record for each rule whether it is enforced by configuration, by a warning message, or only by human review.

Confirm in the engine's configuration that the non-illustrated plan codes from Appendix B cannot produce an illustration at all, and that the illustrated scale cannot be keyed above the disciplined current scale loaded for the plan.

Confirm the state-variable text library holds the state-specific narrative for each of the 45 jurisdictions and that state selection is driven by the situs of the group policy, not the producer's address.
Raise a change request for every rule left on human review only, with a target release, and record the interim manual control in the procedure until the change ships.
checklist.done: every procedure rule is mapped to a system control, a warning or a documented manual control with an open change request.

checklist.step: Run legal and actuarial review of the drafted procedure
actions: Read the draft against the 45-state matrix and confirm each state deviation flagged in the matrix appears as a procedure step or a state variation table entry, not merely as a footnote.
Check every citation in the draft resolves to the state's current adopted text and reject any citation to a superseded version or to the NAIC model where the state has amended it.
Have the illustration actuary confirm the disciplined current scale, self-support and lapse-support wording matches the tests actually run and the ASOP No. 24 language.
Return a consolidated redline to the Compliance Analyst with each comment marked mandatory or advisory, and require written disposition of every mandatory comment.
checklist.done: a legal and actuarial redline exists and every mandatory comment carries a written disposition.

checklist.step: Obtain approval and report the procedure to the compliance committee
actions: Review the final draft with the disposition log of mandatory comments and the list of manual controls still pending system enforcement.
Sign the approval page recording approver name, title, approval date and the effective date of the version.
Table a summary at the compliance committee covering the states with deviations, the open illustration engine change requests and the non-illustrated plan designations.
Record the committee minute reference on the approval page so the approval is traceable at exam.
checklist.done: the version carries a signed, dated approval page and a compliance committee minute reference.

checklist.step: Publish the version, retire the prior one and collect attestations
actions: Load the approved document into the GRC platform policy library under REG-012, set the version number, effective date and next review date, and mark the prior version superseded so it stops returning in search.

Push a read-and-attest task to the distribution list: new business case managers, group underwriters, producer compliance, the illustration engine owner and the illustration actuary, with a 20-business-day due date.
Publish a one-page change summary naming what moved since the last version — new state deviations, changed plan designations, changed wording blacklist entries.
Chase non-attestors at day 10 and day 18 and escalate anyone still open at day 21 to their department head.
checklist.done: the new version is live, the prior version is superseded, and the attestation report shows 100% completion or named escalations.

checklist.step: Run the scheduled annual review against the regulatory change feed
actions: Open the regulatory change feed and extract every bulletin, adopted amendment and NAIC Life Insurance Illustrations Model Regulation revision issued in the 45 jurisdictions since the last review date.
Assess each item as impact / no impact on the procedure, and for impact items name the procedure section to change and the compliance date the state set.
Re-run the state matrix refresh so citations and effective dates match the current text, and re-capture the regulation text where it changed.
Hand the impact list to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager to open the redline cycle by 15 November so approval lands before 31 December.
checklist.done: every jurisdictional change since the last review is assessed, and impact items are handed over with named sections and compliance dates.

checklist.step: File the procedure evidence pack for the retention period
actions: Assemble the pack: approved procedure version, redline against the prior version, legal and actuarial comment disposition log, 45-state matrix with dated text captures, attestation report and committee minute reference.
File it in the compliance evidence repository under REG-012-C01 and the review year, and apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the repository index makes the pack retrievable by state, plan code and review year so a call letter can be answered without a manual trawl.
Record the pack location on the GRC platform control record so the control and its evidence stay linked.
checklist.done: the pack is filed, labelled for 7-year retention, indexed by state and plan code, and linked from the control record.

testing.step: Build the population of jurisdiction requirements the procedure must satisfy
actions: Extract all 45 jurisdiction rows from the Model 582 requirements matrix with citation, effective date, deviation flags and the procedure section each row maps to.
Add every Group Life plan code from Appendix A so a state-by-plan grid, not just a state list, forms the population.
Reconcile the state count to the company's licence register for Group Life and resolve any state licensed but absent from the matrix before sampling.
testing.done: the population is a reconciled state-by-plan grid signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the matrix back to the regulators' own published text
actions: For each of the 45 rows, open the state insurance department's published regulation page and compare the citation and effective date to the matrix row.
List rows where the published text has been amended after the matrix capture date as automatic exceptions.
Confirm the attached dated text capture matches the citation on the row and is not a capture of the NAIC model where the state amended it.
testing.done: every matrix row is reconciled to published state text or listed as a stale-citation exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the state and illustration sample
actions: Take 100% of the states flagged with a deviation from the model plus the representative jurisdiction, Alaska.
Take 12 further states at random using a recorded seed, for a minimum of 20 states in total.
For each sampled state, draw 5 Group Life illustrations produced in the review year from the illustration engine output log, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn by a third party.
testing.done: the sample covers every deviation state and 5 reproducible illustrations per sampled state.

testing.step: Re-perform the state requirement lookup for each sampled jurisdiction
actions: Read the sampled state's adopted illustrations regulation cold and write your own list of its content, annual report, in-force illustration and certification requirements before opening the procedure.
Compare your list to the procedure's state variation table; a requirement the procedure omits is an exception, and so is a procedure step citing the wrong subsection.
Record the subsection you relied on for each requirement and screenshot the text into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state has an independent requirement list, a comparison result and captured source text.

testing.step: Trace the procedure's content rules onto real printed illustrations
actions: Pull each sampled illustration PDF from the document management repository by certificate number.

Tick off, on the printed page, the Model 582 Section 6 elements the procedure claims are printed: the 'Life Insurance Illustration' label, insurer and producer names, plan/form number, generic name, initial death benefit, and the guaranteed / midpoint / illustrated-scale columns.
Check the numeric summary appears at years 5, 10, 20 and age 70 with all three scales, and that year-by-year detail runs for the first 10 years.

Scan the narrative for any word on the banned list — 'vanish', 'vanishing premium', unqualified 'investment' or 'savings' — and treat a hit as a reportable breach rather than a documentation exception.
testing.done: every sampled illustration is ticked against the Section 6 element list with hits on the banned-wording scan recorded separately.

testing.step: Verify the illustrated / non-illustrated designations are actuarially supported
actions: For 5 sampled plan codes, obtain the self-support and lapse-support test output behind the designation and check the test date falls inside the review year.
Confirm the disciplined current scale used in the test is the scale loaded in the illustration engine for that plan, not a later or earlier version.
Confirm no illustration exists in the output log for any plan designated non-illustrated.
Record any plan where the currently payable scale exceeds the disciplined current scale as a Section 4 breach.
testing.done: each sampled plan designation ties to dated test output and to the scale actually loaded in the engine.

testing.step: Test the signature, delivery and retention controls on the sampled illustrations
actions: For each sampled illustration, confirm both the applicant and producer signatures are present and dated on or before the application date.
Where the certificate was issued other than as applied for, confirm a revised conforming illustration exists signed no later than the delivery date.
Where no illustration was used at sale, confirm the producer certification on the application and the illustration delivered at policy delivery.
Check the repository retention label on each document is set to 3 years after the certificate ceases to be in force.
testing.done: every sampled illustration shows the required signatures or certification and the correct retention label.

testing.step: Recompute the review and certification calendar dates
actions: Take the prior version's approval date and confirm the current review completed within 12 months of it.

Recompute the certification path dates: inputs due two weeks before drafting, package due 15 February, commissioner filings by the 1 March annual-statement date in the states that tie them together, and compare each to the actual date achieved.
Confirm the GRC platform reminder tasks for 1 October, 15 November, 31 December and 15 February exist, fired, and were closed by a named person.
Any review or filing completed after its computed date is an exception with the number of days late stated.
testing.done: every calendar date is recomputed against the actual date achieved with days late stated for each miss.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the state or certificate number, the requirement missed and the market conduct exposure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — stale citation, unmapped state deviation, engine configuration gap, missing signature control, late review — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for banned-wording or unsupported-scale breaches, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel the same week.
Carry every open issue into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the procedure test
actions: Compute the coverage rate — jurisdictions with a mapped, currently cited procedure section divided by 45 — and compare it to the zero-gap threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references supporting it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted no part of the procedure, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any Section 4 breaches to the compliance committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-012-C01.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with coverage rate, stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Compliance procedure documented.value: MCAS Life Submission Procedure — participation test by state, element-by-element data mapping, validation error disposition, officer attestation, resubmission and state inquiry handling

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Statutory Reporting Manager; re-approved every year once the NAIC publishes the new data-year Data Call and Definitions

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: One deadline per data year — the Life MCAS submission is due 30 April following the data year; states granting an extension record the extended date on the tracker, and the participation test is run in January on prior-year premium

Deadline reminders configured.value: Reminders at 15 January (participation test), 1 March (first full extract loaded), 1 April (validation clean), 20 April (officer attestation) and 29 April (submission confirmed) for every participating state

checklist.step: Run the participation test to fix which states must be filed
actions: Pull direct written premium for Group Life by state and writing company for the data year from the statutory annual statement Schedule T and the state page.
Apply the MCAS participation threshold from the current Data Call and Definitions to each state-company pair and mark it in scope or out of scope, recording the premium figure used.
Cross-check the result against the state list published in the NAIC MCAS call letters and against last year's participating states, and investigate every state that changed status.
Publish the participating state-company matrix to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager by 15 January.
checklist.done: a dated participation matrix names every state-company pair in scope with the premium figure that put it there.

checklist.step: Read the current data-year Data Call and Definitions and diff it against last year
actions: Download the current NAIC MCAS Life Data Call and Definitions document from the MCAS page on iSite+ and the accompanying state-specific call letters.
Diff it against the prior data year and list every added, removed or re-defined element, every changed interrogatory and every changed validation rule.
For each change, name the source system field that must now feed it and the owner who has to supply it.
Circulate the change list to the Data Quality Analyst, the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Claims Director / Manager with a 1 March deadline for mapping confirmation.
checklist.done: the year-over-year change list is issued with a source field and an owner against every changed element.

checklist.step: Map every reported element to a source system field
actions: Build the mapping sheet with one row per MCAS element: element name, definition text, source system, table and column, filter logic, and the owner who signs the mapping.

Map the illustration-sensitive elements with particular care — policies issued, internal and external replacements, surrenders and lapses within the first 13 months — since these are the elements a Model 582 market analyst reads first.
Encode the data-year boundary rules exactly as defined: transaction date versus effective date, and the treatment of certificates issued and terminated inside the same data year.
Have each source system owner sign the rows drawn from their system before the extract is coded.
checklist.done: every MCAS element has a signed mapping row with source table, column and filter logic.

checklist.step: Extract the Group Life certificate population for the data year
actions: Run the MCAS extract job against the policy administration system for the data year, split by state of certificate situs and writing company.
Produce the counts the data call requires: certificates in force at year end, issued during the year, replaced, surrendered, lapsed, and those lapsed within 13 months of issue.
Reconcile in-force certificate counts to the statutory annual statement Exhibit of Life Insurance and resolve every difference above 0.5% before the file moves on.
Load the extract into the MCAS staging tables in the data warehouse and record the job run id and row counts.
checklist.done: the certificate extract is loaded, split by state and company, and reconciled to the annual statement within tolerance.

checklist.step: Extract the claims and complaint elements and align their definitions
actions: Extract Group Life death claims for the data year by state: received, paid, denied, closed without payment, and open at year end, with the days-to-pay buckets the data call defines.
Confirm the claim date used matches the data call definition — date of receipt of due proof of death, not date of first notice — and re-run if the wrong field was used.
Take the complaint counts from the complaints register split into those received directly and those received via a department of insurance, matched to the same state and data year.
Hand both extracts to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst with a written statement of the definitions applied.
checklist.done: claims and complaint counts are extracted on the data call's own definitions with the definitions stated in writing.

checklist.step: Run internal data-quality checks before touching the NAIC application
actions: Run the ratio checks a market analyst would run: replacement ratio, 13-month lapse ratio, claim denial ratio and complaint ratio per state, and compare each to the company's prior two data years.
Investigate every state where a ratio moved more than 20% year over year and record the business explanation on the state row before submission, not after a regulator asks.
Run the completeness checks: no negative counts, no state in the participation matrix with a null file, sub-counts summing to their totals.
Produce the data-quality report and route it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for review by 1 April.
checklist.done: the data-quality report is issued with a written explanation on every state ratio that moved more than 20%.

checklist.step: Load the data into the NAIC MCAS application and clear its validations
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ with the company's MCAS user account and open the MCAS application for the current data year and the Life line of business.
Upload the state file for each participating state-company pair in the required layout, or key the values into the online blank where the state count is small.
Work the validation report to zero blocking errors, and for each warning either correct the data or enter the explanatory comment the application requires.
Save the validation log and the cleared-warning comments to the submission folder as evidence of what was explained and why.
checklist.done: every participating state file is loaded with zero blocking errors and every warning either corrected or explained on the record.

checklist.step: Answer the MCAS interrogatories on illustration and sales practice
actions: Read each interrogatory in the current data call and draft the answer from the approved Life Insurance Illustration Compliance Procedure rather than from memory.
Where an interrogatory asks about producer training, suitability review or replacement handling, cite the procedure section and the control that evidences it.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any answer that concedes a gap, and pair the concession with the remediation already underway and its target date.
Record the final answers and their supporting references in the submission folder so the same answer is reproducible next year.
checklist.done: every interrogatory answer is drafted from a cited procedure section and cleared where it concedes a gap.

checklist.step: Reconcile the assembled submission to the statutory annual statement
actions: Compare MCAS direct written premium by state to the statutory annual statement state page and Schedule T for the same writing company.
Compare in-force certificate counts to the Exhibit of Life Insurance and claim counts to the claim exhibits.
Document every difference with its cause — timing, definitional difference between MCAS and statutory, or a genuine data error — and correct the error class before submission.
Sign the reconciliation sheet and file it with the submission package.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation explains every MCAS-to-annual-statement difference by cause.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer attestation
actions: Assemble the attestation pack: final data by state, data-quality report, annual statement reconciliation, validation log and the interrogatory answers.
Walk the authorised officer through the material year-over-year movements and the explanations recorded against them.
Have the officer complete the attestation in the NAIC MCAS application for each state-company submission, recording name, title and date.
Capture the attestation screens into the submission folder before any file is transmitted.
checklist.done: a dated officer attestation exists for every state-company submission with the pack that supported it.

checklist.step: Submit every participating state by the 30 April deadline and capture the confirmations
actions: Submit each state-company filing in the MCAS application and wait for the status to move to Submitted before starting the next.
Download or screenshot the submission confirmation showing state, company, line of business, data year and submission timestamp.
Tick each state off the participation matrix as submitted and chase any state left open at 29 April with the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Where a state granted an extension, file the extension approval alongside the confirmation so the later date is defensible.
checklist.done: every participating state shows a captured submission confirmation dated on or before 30 April or a filed extension approval.

checklist.step: Handle post-submission state inquiries and resubmissions
actions: Monitor the MCAS application and the regulatory mailbox for state data-quality inquiries and requests to explain outlier ratios.
Answer within the state's stated response window, quoting the extract logic and the source counts rather than restating the reported figure.
Where a correction is agreed, request the state's permission to resubmit, reload the corrected file and capture the new confirmation.
Log every resubmission in the GRC platform with the element corrected, the old and new values, the cause and the date.
checklist.done: every state inquiry has a dated response and every agreed correction has a logged, confirmed resubmission.

checklist.step: Feed the submitted ratios back into market conduct monitoring
actions: Load the submitted MCAS ratios by state into the market conduct dashboard alongside the company's quarterly internal metrics.
Highlight the states where the company's replacement, 13-month lapse or complaint ratio sits in the worst quartile of the NAIC's published MCAS ratio ranges for the line.
Open a monitoring item for each worst-quartile state naming the likely driver — producer concentration, illustration practice, group takeover activity — and an owner.
Brief the compliance committee on the exposure since worst-quartile MCAS ratios are the usual trigger for a state market analysis review.
checklist.done: submitted ratios are on the dashboard and every worst-quartile state has an owned monitoring item.

checklist.step: Close the cycle with a post-submission lessons-learned review
actions: Run a review in May with the Data Quality Analyst, claims and policy admin owners covering every validation error, late input and manual workaround used this cycle.
Convert each recurring manual workaround into a change request against the extract code or the source system, with an owner and a target date ahead of the next 1 March extract.
Update the mapping sheet and the submission procedure with what actually happened, so next year's analyst inherits the fix rather than the folklore.
Record the actions on the GRC platform control record for REG-012-C02.
checklist.done: a lessons-learned record exists with owned, dated change requests against the extract or source systems.

checklist.step: File the submission evidence pack for retention
actions: Assemble the pack: participation matrix, mapping sheet, final data files, validation logs, data-quality report, annual statement reconciliation, interrogatory answers, attestations and per-state submission confirmations.
File it in the compliance evidence repository under REG-012-C02 and the data year, and apply the 7-year retention label.
Index the pack by state, writing company and data year so a single-state MCAS inquiry can be answered without reopening the warehouse.
Link the pack from the GRC platform control record and from the market conduct exam readiness file.
checklist.done: the pack is filed, retained for 7 years, indexed by state and data year and linked from the exam readiness file.

testing.step: Rebuild the population of states that should have been filed
actions: Independently pull Group Life direct written premium by state and writing company from the statutory annual statement state pages for the data year.
Apply the current data call's participation threshold yourself and build your own list of states that should have been filed.
Compare your list to the company's participation matrix and treat any state on yours but not theirs as a missed filing, not a scoping difference.
testing.done: an independently built participating-state list exists and every difference from the company's matrix is listed.

testing.step: Reconcile submitted values to the source of record
actions: Take the final submitted data file for each state and compare each element to the MCAS staging table the extract produced.
Compare staging totals up to the statutory annual statement Exhibit of Life Insurance and the claim exhibits for the same company.
Record differences per element in absolute and percentage terms and mark anything above the 0.5% tolerance, or any policy-count difference at all, as an exception.
testing.done: every submitted element is reconciled to staging and to the annual statement with differences quantified.

testing.step: Draw the sample of states and underlying certificate records
actions: Take 100% of states whose reported ratios moved more than 20% year over year and 100% of states that required a resubmission.
Take 8 further states at random on a recorded seed, for a minimum of 12 states.
Within each sampled state draw 25 certificate records across the issued, replaced, surrendered and 13-month-lapse buckets, seeded and reproducible.
Document the seed, the population sizes and the draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all outlier and resubmitted states plus a reproducible random draw and per-state record sample.

testing.step: Re-perform the element classification on the sampled records
actions: Open each sampled certificate in the policy administration system and read the transaction history yourself.

Classify it against the data call definitions — issued, internal replacement, external replacement, surrender, lapse, lapse within 13 months of issue — without looking at how the extract classified it.
Compare to the extract's classification; a misclassified replacement or a lapse counted outside the 13-month window is an exception even if the state total happens to tie.
Screenshot the transaction history relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled record has an independent classification, a comparison result and a captured transaction history.

testing.step: Trace the claims and complaint elements back to case records
actions: For 15 sampled death claims, read the claim file and confirm the date of receipt of due proof of death used in the days-to-pay bucket matches the file.
Confirm the paid, denied and closed-without-payment classification in the extract matches the claim disposition recorded in the system.
For 10 sampled complaints, confirm the direct versus department-of-insurance split matches the intake channel recorded on the complaint record.
List every classification difference with the state and the element it distorted.
testing.done: sampled claims and complaints are traced to case records with every classification difference listed.

testing.step: Verify submission timing and the officer attestation for every state
actions: Open each captured submission confirmation and read the submission timestamp, the state, the writing company, the line of business and the data year.
Compute days late as submission date minus 30 April, using the extension date only where an extension approval is on file.
Confirm an officer attestation with name, title and date exists for each state-company submission and pre-dates the submission timestamp.
Any state without a confirmation, or attested after submission, is an exception.
testing.done: every state has a confirmation, a computed days-late figure and an attestation pre-dating the submission.

testing.step: Review the validation log and the explanations given to the NAIC application
actions: Read the saved validation log for each sampled state and list every warning cleared by comment rather than by correction.
Test each explanatory comment against the underlying data and flag any comment that is unsupported or that restates the reported figure without explaining it.
Confirm no blocking error was bypassed by re-keying a value that the source data does not support.
testing.done: every warning cleared by comment is tested and unsupported explanations are listed.

testing.step: Recompute the reported ratios and compare them to the benchmark ranges
actions: Recompute replacement ratio, 13-month lapse ratio, claim denial ratio and complaint ratio per sampled state from the submitted numerators and denominators.
Compare each to the value the company reported on its dashboard and to the NAIC's published MCAS ratio ranges for the Life line.
Confirm every worst-quartile state has an owned monitoring item as the procedure requires.
Report any state where the recomputed ratio differs from the dashboard value as a reporting-integrity exception.
testing.done: ratios are recomputed per sampled state, benchmarked, and every worst-quartile state is confirmed to carry a monitoring item.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the state, writing company, element and the reported versus tested value.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — participation test error, mapping error, definition misread, source data defect, late input, missed submission — and an owner.
Set a remediation date, and where the correct value would change a reported ratio materially, require a resubmission request to the state.
Carry every open issue into next data year's pre-submission dry run as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where material, a resubmission request.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the MCAS test
actions: Compute on-time submission rate across participating states and the element reconciliation exception rate, and compare both to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who built no part of the extract, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any missed state to the compliance committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-012-C02.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with on-time rate, exception rate, stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed.

checklist.step: Define the illustration conduct metric set and its formulas
actions: Write one definition card per metric: signed-illustration completeness rate, replacement ratio, 13-month lapse ratio, illustration-related complaint rate per 1,000 certificates in force, in-force illustration 30-day turnaround rate, annual report production completeness, and producer illustration exception rate.
State each formula as an explicit numerator and denominator with the date field that assigns a record to the quarter, so two analysts get the same number.

Tie each metric back to the Model 582 obligation it monitors — Section 6 signature, Section 7 annual report and in-force illustration, Section 4 prohibited practices — so the scorecard is defensible as a compliance control rather than an MI pack.
Have the Data Quality Analyst sign each card confirming the source fields exist and are populated for all 45 jurisdictions.
checklist.done: every metric has a signed definition card with formula, date field and the Model 582 obligation it monitors.

checklist.step: Set the amber and red thresholds against external benchmarks
actions: Take the current NAIC MCAS Life published ratio ranges for replacement, lapse and complaint metrics and locate the company's last submitted position within them.
Set red at the worst-quartile boundary of the published range or the company's prior-year value plus 20%, whichever is tighter, and amber one step inside it.

For the internally defined metrics — signed-illustration completeness, in-force illustration turnaround, annual report completeness — set red at any shortfall from 100% and amber at 99.5%, since these are absolute statutory duties.
Record the source and date of every benchmark on the threshold sheet and have the Head of Compliance approve it for the year.
checklist.done: an approved threshold sheet exists with a dated external source or statutory basis behind each amber and red level.

checklist.step: Build the quarterly data cut from the source systems
actions: Schedule the cut for the 5th working day after quarter end, pulling Group Life certificate transactions from the policy administration system, complaints from the complaints register and illustration events from the illustration engine output log.
Key every record to state of group policy situs and to the servicing producer number so both drill-downs are possible without a re-run.
Snapshot the cut into a dated, immutable table so the quarter's published numbers can be reproduced after later data movement.
Publish row counts and the job run id to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager with the cut.
checklist.done: a dated immutable quarterly cut exists, keyed by state and producer, with row counts published.

checklist.step: Reconcile the cut before any metric is computed
actions: Reconcile in-force certificate counts in the cut to the policy administration system's own quarter-end in-force report and resolve any difference above 0.5%.
Reconcile complaint counts to the complaints register total for the quarter and to any complaints received via a state department of insurance.
Check state coverage: all 45 jurisdictions with in-force Group Life business must appear, and a state with zero records must be confirmed as genuinely zero rather than dropped by a join.
Sign the reconciliation sheet and attach it to the cut before the scorecard is built.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation ties the cut to system totals with full 45-jurisdiction coverage confirmed.

checklist.step: Compute the metrics and publish the scorecard
actions: Compute each metric strictly on its signed definition card and publish it at enterprise, state and producer level in the market conduct scorecard.
Colour each cell against the approved threshold sheet and show the prior four quarters alongside so a trend, not a point, drives the reading.
Add a drill-through from any red cell to the underlying certificate, complaint or illustration records so an investigator starts on the data rather than on a re-extract request.
Publish by the 10th working day after quarter end and record the publication timestamp.
checklist.done: the scorecard is published by the 10th working day with state and producer drill-through on every red cell.

checklist.step: Investigate every red breach at state level
actions: For each red state cell, drill through to the records and identify the concentration — a single group takeover, one producer, one plan code, or a genuine broad shift.
Pull 10 underlying certificates and read the signed illustration, the application and the replacement paperwork to see whether the metric reflects a conduct problem or a data artefact.
Write the finding on the breach record with the concentration identified, the sample evidence and the conclusion.
Where the driver is a conduct problem, hand it to the Producer Compliance Manager or the Policy Admin Ops Lead with a named action and a date.
checklist.done: every red state cell has a written investigation naming the concentration, the sampled evidence and a conclusion.

checklist.step: Run the producer-level outlier review
actions: Rank producers by replacement ratio, 13-month lapse ratio and illustration exception rate, restricted to producers with at least 25 Group Life certificates in the quarter so small volumes do not dominate the list.

Take the top 20 outliers and pull each one's illustration output log entries, checking for illustrations produced outside the company engine, unsigned illustrations and supplemental illustrations delivered without a basic illustration.
Interview the top 5 outliers' distribution managers and record the explanation and the agreed action against each producer.
Apply the consequence ladder from the illustration procedure — coaching, mandatory retraining, suspension of new business authority — and record the step applied and its date.
checklist.done: the top 20 producer outliers are reviewed with a recorded explanation and a consequence-ladder step applied where warranted.

checklist.step: Check the in-force illustration and annual report service metrics
actions: Pull the in-force illustration request queue for the quarter and compute the elapsed days from request receipt to illustration despatch for every request.
List every request that breached the 30-day service level with the certificate number, the days taken and the reason, and confirm the illustration was ultimately delivered.
Reconcile the annual report production run count to the in-force certificate count at the run date, and list any certificate that received no report.
Confirm the underfunding warning required by Model 582 Section 7 was printed on every report where the current scale would not keep the certificate in force to the next report.
checklist.done: every in-force illustration request has an elapsed-days figure and the annual report run reconciles to the in-force population.

checklist.step: Test the illustration-related complaint slice
actions: Filter the quarter's complaints for the illustration cause codes — projected values not achieved, premium offset or 'vanishing premium' expectation, non-guaranteed element reduction, misleading sales presentation.
For each, read the complaint file and the signed illustration held for the certificate and record whether the illustration as signed supports or contradicts the complainant's expectation.
Group the findings by producer, plan code and state to expose a pattern rather than a run of individual cases.
Escalate any complaint where the signed illustration is missing, altered or non-conforming as a Model 582 breach rather than a service complaint.
checklist.done: every illustration-cause complaint is read against its signed illustration and grouped by producer, plan and state.

checklist.step: Log breaches as issues and assign remediation
actions: Raise a GRC issue within 2 business days of the data cut for every red threshold breach, naming the metric, the state or producer, the value and the threshold.
Attach the investigation write-up, the sampled evidence and the agreed action to the issue.
Set an owner and a remediation date proportionate to the exposure — 30 days for a producer sanction, 90 days for a system or process change.
Link each issue to the REG-012 control record so the exam readiness file picks it up automatically.
checklist.done: every red breach has a GRC issue raised within 2 business days with evidence, owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Report the scorecard to the compliance committee
actions: Table the scorecard by the 15th working day after quarter end with the red and amber cells, the investigations and the open issue ageing.
Call out the states whose ratios would land in the worst quartile of the published MCAS ranges, since those are the states most likely to open a market analysis review.
Record committee decisions — accept, remediate, escalate to the board risk committee — against each red item in the minutes.
Carry unresolved reds forward as standing items until closed rather than letting them drop out of the next pack.
checklist.done: the committee minute records a decision against every red item and unresolved reds are carried forward as standing items.

checklist.step: Feed confirmed conduct findings back into the illustration procedure and training
actions: Take the confirmed conduct findings from the quarter's investigations and turn each into a worked example for the Group Life illustration course.
Assign targeted refresher modules to the producers and case managers named in the findings with a 30-day completion window.
Ask the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager to raise a procedure change request where a finding shows the procedure itself was silent or ambiguous.
Report completion rates for the targeted assignments back to the Producer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: each confirmed finding produces a training example, a targeted assignment and, where needed, a procedure change request.

checklist.step: Re-baseline thresholds when the benchmark or the book changes
actions: Once the new NAIC MCAS ratio publication is available, reset the external thresholds against the current ranges and record the new source date.
Reassess thresholds after any material book change — a large group takeover, a plan withdrawal, entry into a new state — since the old denominator no longer describes the book.
Document every threshold change with the reason, the old and new values and the effective quarter so a trend break is explainable at exam.
Route the revised threshold sheet to the Head of Compliance for approval before it is applied.
checklist.done: threshold changes are documented with reason, old and new values, effective quarter and an approval.

checklist.step: Verify the scorecard data lineage each quarter
actions: Confirm in the data catalog that every scorecard field still resolves to the source column named on its definition card.
Re-run the lineage check after any release to the policy administration system, the complaints register or the illustration engine, since a renamed field silently zeroes a metric.
Compare this quarter's row counts and null rates per field to the prior quarter and investigate any change above 10%.
Sign the lineage check and file it with the quarter's cut.
checklist.done: a signed lineage check confirms every scorecard field's source column and flags any material null-rate movement.

checklist.step: File the quarterly monitoring pack for retention
actions: Assemble the pack: definition cards, approved threshold sheet, the dated data cut, reconciliation, published scorecard, breach investigations, producer outlier review and the committee minute reference.
File it in the compliance evidence repository under REG-012-C03 and the quarter, with the 7-year retention label.
Index by state, producer number and quarter so a state market analyst's question about one quarter's ratio can be answered directly.
Link the pack from the market conduct exam readiness file.
checklist.done: the quarterly pack is filed, retained 7 years, indexed by state and producer and linked from the exam readiness file.

testing.step: Rebuild the population of quarterly monitoring cycles and their inputs
actions: List the quarterly monitoring packs filed for the period under test and confirm one exists per quarter with no gaps.
For each quarter, take the dated immutable data cut and record its row counts, state coverage and job run id.
Confirm the cut covers all 45 jurisdictions with in-force Group Life business and note any state absent from any quarter.
testing.done: every quarter in the test period has a pack, a dated cut and confirmed 45-jurisdiction coverage.

testing.step: Reconcile the monitoring cut to the source systems independently
actions: Pull your own quarter-end in-force certificate count and quarterly transaction counts from the policy administration system.
Compare them to the numbers in the monitoring cut and quantify each difference as a percentage.
Do the same for the complaints register total and the illustration engine output log count.
Anything above 0.5% that the company's own reconciliation did not identify is an exception.
testing.done: the cut is independently reconciled to policy, complaint and illustration source counts with differences quantified.

testing.step: Draw the sample of metrics, states and producers
actions: Take 100% of red threshold breaches across the tested quarters and 100% of the states that appeared in the worst quartile of the published MCAS ranges.
Take 4 metrics at random from the definition card set and 10 states at random on a recorded seed.
Take 15 producers from the outlier review, weighted to those who received a consequence-ladder step.
Record the seed, the population sizes and the draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers every red breach and worst-quartile state plus a reproducible random draw of metrics, states and producers.

testing.step: Recompute the sampled metrics from the raw cut
actions: Take each sampled metric's signed definition card and write the numerator and denominator query yourself against the dated cut.
Compare your result to the published scorecard value at enterprise, state and producer level.
Any difference above 1% is an exception; investigate whether the cause is the query, the date field, or a scorecard filter not described on the definition card.
Record both queries and both results in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled metric is recomputed from the raw cut with differences above 1% investigated to a cause.

testing.step: Re-perform a red breach investigation from the records up
actions: For 5 sampled red breaches, drill to the underlying certificates and reach your own view of the driver before reading the company's investigation write-up.
Pull 10 certificates per breach and read the signed illustration, the application and any replacement paperwork.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded one; a breach written off as a data artefact where the records show missing or non-conforming illustrations is a reportable exception.
Capture the records relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled breach has an independent conclusion drawn from certificate records and compared to the recorded one.

testing.step: Test the escalation and issue-logging timing
actions: For every red breach in the tested quarters, find the GRC issue and read its creation timestamp.
Compute elapsed business days from the data cut date to issue creation and compare to the 2-business-day requirement.
Confirm each issue names the metric, the state or producer, the value, the threshold, an owner and a remediation date, with no blank fields.
List red breaches with no issue at all as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every red breach has an issue with a computed escalation lag and no missing fields, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Verify producer sanctions were actually applied
actions: For the sampled producers who reached a consequence-ladder step, confirm the recorded action was executed — coaching note filed, retraining assigned and completed, or new business authority actually suspended in the producer record.
Check the suspension date against the date new business stopped flowing from that producer in the policy administration system.
Confirm any producer terminated for illustration misconduct has the termination reason recorded so it can be reported on future appointment terminations.
A recorded sanction with no system effect is an exception.
testing.done: every sampled sanction is traced to an executed action with a matching system effect and date.

testing.step: Recompute the service-level and completeness maths
actions: For 20 sampled in-force illustration requests, recompute elapsed days from request receipt to despatch and compare to the 30-day service level and to the reported turnaround rate.
Recompute annual report completeness as reports produced divided by in-force certificates at the run date and compare to the published figure.
For 10 certificates whose current scale would not sustain them to the next report, confirm the Model 582 Section 7 underfunding warning actually printed.
Any missing warning is a reportable breach rather than a metric exception.
testing.done: turnaround and completeness maths are recomputed and the underfunding warning is confirmed on every tested certificate.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the quarter, the metric or breach, the published versus recomputed value and the exposure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — definition drift, lineage break, late cut, unlogged breach, unexecuted sanction, missing statutory warning — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require the affected quarter's scorecard to be restated where a metric was materially wrong.
Carry every open issue into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where material, a scorecard restatement.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the monitoring test
actions: Compute the metric accuracy rate and the on-time escalation rate across the tested quarters and compare both to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who built no part of the scorecard and investigated no sampled breach, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any unlogged red breach to the compliance committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under REG-012-C03.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with accuracy rate, escalation rate, stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed.
