checklist.step: Build the file index from the Handbook standards that apply to Group Life illustrations
actions: Work through the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook life marketing and sales examination standards and list the ones an illustration-focused exam will test — advertising and sales material control, producer licensing and appointment, illustration delivery and signature, replacement handling, complaint handling, and annual report and disclosure.
Create one file section per standard with a stated purpose, the artefacts it must hold, the named owner and the refresh cadence.
Map each section to the corresponding Model 582 sections as adopted in Alaska and the other 44 jurisdictions, so a state-specific request routes to the right section without a search.
Publish the index to the section owners and get each owner's written acceptance of their section.
checklist.done: the index lists every applicable Handbook standard as a file section with artefacts, an accepting owner and a refresh cadence.

checklist.step: Populate the illustration artefact section and prove retrievability
actions: Confirm signed basic illustrations are indexed in the document management repository by certificate number, group policy number, state, producer number and illustration date.
Run a retrieval test: pick 25 certificates at random across 10 states and pull the signed illustration within 15 minutes each, recording the time taken and any failure.
Where a certificate was issued other than as applied for, confirm the revised conforming illustration is filed alongside the original.
Record the retention label on each document — 3 years after the certificate is no longer in force per Model 582 Section 10 — and confirm no in-scope document is on a shorter label.
checklist.done: the retrieval test returns every sampled signed illustration within the target time and every document carries the correct retention label.

checklist.step: Keep the illustration actuary and officer certifications current in the file
actions: File the current-year illustration actuary certification with the self-support and lapse-support test output, the experience study behind the disciplined current scale, and the ASOP No. 24 conformity statement.
File the accompanying officer certification confirming the illustration actuary was given the access and information needed.
File the board minute reference showing the certification was presented, and the per-state filing confirmations for the commissioners.
Hold the prior three years' certifications in the same section, since examiners routinely look back across the scope period.
checklist.done: the section holds the current and prior three years' certifications with test output, board minute reference and state filing confirmations.

checklist.step: Keep producer licensing and appointment evidence exam-ready
actions: Run the NIPR producer database reconciliation monthly against the company's appointed-producer register for all 45 jurisdictions.

List producers who wrote Group Life business in a state where the licence or appointment was not effective on the application date — this is the single finding examiners raise most often alongside illustration defects.
File the monthly reconciliation output, the exception list and the resolution of each exception in the file section.
Confirm appointment termination records carry the reason code, since illustration misconduct terminations must be reportable.
checklist.done: the section holds monthly NIPR reconciliations with every unlicensed or unappointed writing exception resolved and evidenced.

checklist.step: Keep the advertising and sales material approval file current
actions: Maintain the advertising register with one row per piece: piece id, media, states of use, first and last use dates, approver and approval date.
Attach the approved final version of each piece and the compliance review note showing the Model 582 prohibited-wording check was performed.
Include producer-generated material submitted for approval and record the disposition of anything rejected, since rejected-but-used material is a classic exam finding.
Retain each piece and its approval for the period the state requires — commonly the greater of the state's advertising retention rule and 3 years from last use.
checklist.done: every advertising piece in the register has an approved version, a prohibited-wording check note and a retention date.

checklist.step: Keep the complaint register and its illustration slice exam-ready
actions: Maintain the register in the format examiners request: complaint number, date received, source (direct or department of insurance), state, certificate number, cause code, disposition, resolution date and elapsed days.
Flag the illustration cause codes so the illustration slice can be produced as a standalone extract on request.
Confirm every complaint file holds the acknowledgement letter, the substantive response and the closing letter, with the state's response deadline met.
Reconcile the register to the complaint counts reported in MCAS for the same period and explain any difference in the file.
checklist.done: the register is in examiner format, the illustration slice extracts cleanly, and it reconciles to the MCAS complaint counts.

checklist.step: Keep training and supervision evidence in the file
actions: File the current Group Life illustration course content, the assignment roster built from the appointed-producer extract, and completion records with dates and scores.
File the escalation record for non-completers showing the consequence-ladder step applied and its date.
Include new-hire onboarding records for case managers and group underwriters covering illustration handling.
Refresh the section quarterly so completion figures in the file never trail the live system by more than a quarter.
checklist.done: the section holds current course content, roster, completion records with dates and the non-completer escalation record.

checklist.step: Keep the prior exam and prior finding history in the file
actions: File every prior market conduct exam report for the 45 jurisdictions with its findings, the company's response, the corrective action plan and the closing letter.
For each prior finding, file the evidence that the corrective action was implemented and is still operating — examiners test prior findings first.
Cross-reference any prior finding that touches illustrations to the current illustration procedure section that now addresses it.
Record any regulatory settlement agreement, consent order or fine with its terms and its ongoing obligations.
checklist.done: every prior exam and finding has its report, response, corrective action evidence and closing letter in the file.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly full-file completeness sweep
actions: Walk the index section by section and record for each: last refresh date, owner, artefact count and whether it is inside its stated cadence.
Mark any section stale by more than one quarter or missing an owner as a gap and raise a GRC issue against the owner with a 30-day fix date.
Spot-check three sections by pulling one artefact each and confirming it opens, is legible and is the current version.
Report the sweep result to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager with a section-level red/amber/green view.
checklist.done: the sweep records refresh date, owner and cadence status for every section, with a GRC issue raised on every gap.

checklist.step: Rehearse a call letter response before one arrives
actions: Once a year, run a mock call letter for one state using a real prior call letter as the template, with a 30-day clock.

Produce the standard opening deliverables: company profile, organisational chart, policy and procedure manuals, in-force and issued Group Life listings for the scope period, complaint register, producer listing and advertising register.
Time each deliverable and record which ones needed a manual build rather than a standing extract.
Convert every manual build into a standing saved extract before the next rehearsal.
checklist.done: the rehearsal produces every standard deliverable inside 30 days with the manual builds converted into standing extracts.

checklist.step: Stand up the exam coordination protocol on receipt of a call letter
actions: Acknowledge the call letter to the examiner-in-charge within 5 business days, confirming the scope period, the lines of business, the exam type and the single point of contact.
Open an exam workspace holding the call letter, the scope, every information request and every response, with a due-date tracker per request.
Brief every section owner on the scope and instruct that no artefact leaves the company except through the exam coordinator.
Agree the delivery mechanism and the confidentiality treatment with the examiner, and record the state's confidentiality statute the company is relying on.
checklist.done: the call letter is acknowledged within 5 business days and an exam workspace with a request tracker and a single contact is live.

checklist.step: Answer examiner information requests within the set windows
actions: Log each information request with its number, text, examiner due date and the file section that answers it.
Pull the response from the standing file rather than from a fresh system query wherever the file already holds it, and note where the file fell short so it can be fixed.
Have Regulatory Counsel review every response for privilege and for statements about past practice before it is sent.
Send through the agreed channel, capture the transmission confirmation and record the sent date against the request.
checklist.done: every information request has a logged due date, a counsel-reviewed response and a captured transmission confirmation on or before its due date.

checklist.step: Manage examiner sample requests and the illustration file pulls
actions: Take the examiner's sample list of certificate numbers and pull each file complete: application, signed basic illustration, any revised conforming illustration, delivery receipt, replacement paperwork and the annual reports issued.
Log any certificate where an artefact cannot be produced, with the reason, before the file goes to the examiner — a surprise gap found by the examiner is worse than a disclosed one.
Produce the files in the examiner's requested order and format with a manifest listing what each file contains.
Keep a complete copy of everything produced in the exam workspace so the record of what was handed over is exact.
checklist.done: every sampled certificate file is produced with a manifest, and every unproducible artefact is disclosed with its reason.

checklist.step: Track criticisms raised during fieldwork and respond before the draft report
actions: Log each examiner criticism or comment form with its date, the standard cited, the assertion and the response due date.
Assemble the factual rebuttal or the acceptance with evidence, and get Regulatory Counsel sign-off before responding.
Where the criticism is accepted, start the corrective action immediately rather than waiting for the final report, and record the start date in the response.
Keep a running criticism log so the draft report can be checked against what was actually raised in fieldwork.
checklist.done: every criticism has a logged, counsel-cleared response and, where accepted, a corrective action already started.

checklist.step: Close the exam out and fold the lessons back into the standing file
actions: File the final report, the company response, the corrective action plan and the closing letter in the prior exam section.
Record for each information request how long the answer took and whether it came from the standing file or a manual build, and fix every section that forced a manual build.
Update the file index where the exam tested something the index did not anticipate.
Report the exam outcome, the open corrective actions and the file improvements to the compliance committee and the board risk committee.
checklist.done: the exam record is filed, every manual-build section is fixed, the index is updated and the outcome is reported to committee.

testing.step: Build the population of file sections and applicable Handbook standards
actions: Extract the exam readiness file index with section name, mapped Handbook standard, owner, stated cadence and last refresh date.
Independently list the Handbook life marketing and sales standards that apply to an illustration-focused Group Life exam.
Compare the two lists and record every applicable standard with no file section as a coverage gap before sampling.
testing.done: the population is the mapped section list with every unmapped applicable standard recorded as a coverage gap.

testing.step: Reconcile the file's underlying registers to the source systems
actions: Compare the in-force and issued Group Life listings held in the file to a fresh extract from the policy administration system for the same scope period and state set.
Compare the complaint register in the file to the complaints register system total and to the counts reported in MCAS.
Compare the producer listing in the file to the appointed-producer register and to the latest NIPR reconciliation.
Quantify every difference and treat a file register that no longer matches its source as stale, regardless of its recorded refresh date.
testing.done: each register in the file is reconciled to its source system with differences quantified and staleness identified.

testing.step: Draw the sample of sections, certificates and information requests
actions: Take 100% of sections marked stale in the last quarterly sweep and 100% of sections mapped to a prior exam finding.
Take 6 further sections at random on a recorded seed.
Draw 30 certificates across 10 states for a retrieval test and, where an exam ran in the period, take 100% of information requests.
Record the seed, population sizes and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all stale and prior-finding sections plus a reproducible draw of sections, certificates and requests.

testing.step: Re-perform the retrieval test on sampled certificates
actions: For each sampled certificate, search the document management repository by certificate number and time how long the signed basic illustration takes to retrieve.
Confirm the document is legible, carries both applicant and producer signatures with dates, and matches the plan and face amount on the certificate record.
Where the certificate was issued other than as applied for, confirm the revised conforming illustration is present.
Record every failed or slow retrieval with the certificate number and the reason.
testing.done: every sampled certificate has a timed retrieval result and a signature and content check, with failures listed.

testing.step: Verify the certification section against the actuary's own records
actions: Confirm the current and prior three years' illustration actuary certifications are present, signed and dated.
Trace the self-support and lapse-support test output filed with each certification to the actuarial model run it came from.
Confirm the officer certification accompanies each year and that the board minute reference and the state filing confirmations exist.
A certification with no supporting test output on file is an exception even though the certification itself is signed.
testing.done: each certification year is complete with signed certifications, traced test output, board reference and filing confirmations.

testing.step: Test producer licensing evidence for the sampled certificates
actions: For each sampled certificate, take the writing producer number and check the licence and appointment status in the state of issue as at the application date.
Compare to the monthly NIPR reconciliation held in the file and confirm any exception on that date was identified and resolved there.
List every certificate written by a producer unlicensed or unappointed on the application date as a reportable breach.
Capture the NIPR result screen for each tested producer into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled certificate's producer status is verified as at the application date with breaches listed and screens captured.

testing.step: Recompute the information request response timing
actions: For each information request in scope, record the receipt date, the examiner due date and the transmission confirmation date.
Recompute elapsed days and days late for each, using the examiner's granted extension only where written evidence of the extension is on file.
Confirm the call letter acknowledgement went out within 5 business days of receipt.
Any request answered late, or answered without a captured transmission confirmation, is an exception.
testing.done: every request has recomputed elapsed and late days against its examiner due date with the acknowledgement timing confirmed.

testing.step: Test whether prior findings genuinely remain remediated
actions: Take every prior exam finding touching illustrations, producer licensing or advertising and read the corrective action the company committed to.
Test the control as it operates today, not as the closing letter described it, using a fresh sample of 10 records per finding.
Confirm the current illustration procedure section cross-referenced to the finding actually addresses it.
A finding whose control has quietly lapsed is a repeat-finding exposure and is reported as such, not as a documentation gap.
testing.done: each prior finding's corrective control is retested on fresh records with lapses reported as repeat-finding exposure.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the file section, the Handbook standard, the artefact missing or stale, and the exam exposure it creates.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — no owner, cadence not run, register drifted from source, indexing failure, late request response, lapsed prior-finding control — and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside 30 days for any section that would be requested in the first exam information request.
Carry every open issue into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, with first-request sections capped at 30 days.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the readiness test
actions: Compute file coverage as populated in-date sections divided by applicable Handbook standards, and the retrieval success rate on the sampled certificates.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no section of the file, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any lapsed prior-finding control and any late examiner response to the compliance committee and file the workpaper under REG-012-C04.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with coverage rate, retrieval success rate, stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the corrective action plan for every Group Life illustration finding raised by a state examiner and reports remediation status to the Head of Compliance and the examiner-in-charge until the state issues its closing letter

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — each finding is re-read against the citing state's own adoption of Model 582 and the Market Regulation Handbook standard the examiner applied, with Alaska taken as the representative text and the Alabama, Arizona and California adoptions checked where the same practice was used in those states

In-scope processes.value: Draft report response, corrective action plan design, illustration process and system fixes, producer retraining or sanction, policyholder restitution where illustrated values were misrepresented, and re-testing to closure

In-scope systems.value: Findings, corrective actions and evidence tracked per finding in the regulatory issue tracker, with the remediated illustration and certificate changes executed in the policy administration system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Market Conduct Finding Remediation Procedure — draft report response, root cause analysis, corrective action design and approval, cross-state read-across, restitution calculation, evidence pack and closure sign-off

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Regulatory Counsel sign-off on the response and restitution sections; reviewed after every closed exam

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven with hard external clocks — written response to the draft examination report within the period the state grants, commonly 30 days of receipt; then each corrective action milestone and any regulatory settlement agreement date, tracked to the state's closing letter

Deadline reminders configured.value: On receipt of a draft report, alerts at day 7, 15 and 25 of the 30-day response window; per corrective action, alerts at 30 days and 7 days before the committed completion date and on any missed date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Draft and final reports, responses, corrective action plans, remediation evidence, restitution registers and closing letters retained 7 years from the closing letter date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every finding is its own tracked record with root cause, affected states and certificates, corrective action, owner, committed date, actual date and closure evidence

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every finding, and Regulatory Counsel clears every written statement made to the examiner and every restitution communication

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every market conduct finding relating to Group Life illustrations open or closed in the period, together with the certificates, producers and restitution payments each corrective action touched

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on the response window — a draft report response after the state's deadline is a fail; every corrective action must complete by its committed date and be evidenced by a re-test, and any restitution shortfall against the recomputed amount is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; the test runs on every finding closure and, for findings open longer than a quarter, at each quarter end until closed

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have designed, executed or signed off any sampled corrective action

Evidence location for test results.value: Per-finding remediation test workpaper (response timing, root cause challenge, re-test results, restitution recomputation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-012-C05

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-finding closure pack — finding text, root cause, corrective action, evidence of implementation, re-test result, restitution register and sign-off — producible to the examiner-in-charge or a follow-up examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager remains the single channel to the examiner-in-charge; Regulatory Counsel clears every response, admission and settlement communication before it is sent

checklist.step: Log the draft report findings and start the response clock
actions: On receipt of the draft examination report, record the receipt date and the state's stated response deadline — commonly 30 days — and set the day 7, 15 and 25 alerts.
Split the report into one tracker record per finding with the exact finding text, the Handbook standard and the state statute or Model 582 section cited, and the error rate the examiner computed.
Assign each finding an owner from the process that produced it — illustration engine, new business, producer compliance, policy administration — not to compliance by default.
Confirm receipt to the examiner-in-charge in writing and state the date the company's response will be delivered.
checklist.done: every finding is a tracker record with cited standard, examiner error rate and a named process owner, and the response date is confirmed to the examiner.

checklist.step: Verify the examiner's sample and error rate before responding
actions: Obtain the examiner's sample list and re-pull each certificate from the policy administration system and the document repository.

Re-perform the test the examiner performed — signed illustration present, conforming content, revised illustration where issued other than as applied for, annual report produced — and record your own result per record.
Recompute the error rate on the examiner's own denominator and compare it to the rate in the draft report.
Where the company's result differs, assemble the specific documents that prove it rather than arguing the methodology.
checklist.done: each sampled record is re-performed, the error rate is recomputed on the examiner's denominator, and differences are evidenced document by document.

checklist.step: Run root cause analysis on each accepted finding
actions: For each finding the company accepts, run a five-whys session with the process owner and record the causal chain, not just the immediate defect.
Classify the root cause: illustration engine configuration, procedure silent or wrong, producer behaviour, training gap, data or indexing failure, or control not operating.
Determine the period the cause was live, since that fixes the population of affected certificates far beyond the examiner's sample.
Record the root cause and the exposure period on the tracker record and have the process owner countersign it.
checklist.done: each accepted finding has a countersigned root cause, a classification and a stated exposure period.

checklist.step: Size the full affected population beyond the examiner's sample
actions: Using the root cause and the exposure period, extract every Group Life certificate that could carry the same defect across all writing companies and states, not only the examined state.
Split the population by state so the read-across to the other Model 582 jurisdictions is explicit and countable.
Test a 50-record sample of the extended population to confirm the defect rate outside the examined state before committing to a remediation scale.
Publish the population size, the state split and the tested defect rate to the Compliance Manager and Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: the full affected population is sized and split by state with a tested defect rate supporting the estimate.

checklist.step: Draft the response to the draft examination report
actions: Draft a finding-by-finding response stating accept, accept in part or contest, with the evidence reference for each position.
For contested findings, cite the specific certificate documents and the state's own regulation text, and avoid disputing the Handbook methodology unless the evidence is decisive.
For accepted findings, state the root cause, the corrective action, the owner and the completion date, and disclose the read-across population rather than waiting to be asked.

Clear the response with the Head of Compliance and, where a settlement or fine is foreseeable, with the General Counsel, then send within the state's response window and capture the transmission confirmation.
checklist.done: a counsel-cleared, finding-by-finding response is sent inside the state's response window with a captured confirmation.

checklist.step: Design the corrective action plan for each finding
actions: For each accepted finding, write the corrective action as discrete deliverables — configuration change, procedure amendment, training assignment, control build, restitution run — each with an owner and a date.
Require every action to name the evidence that will prove completion before work starts, so closure is not argued afterwards.
Set interim controls to run from the response date until the permanent fix ships, and name who performs them and how often.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the plan and share it with the examiner-in-charge where the state expects a plan with the response.
checklist.done: every accepted finding has an approved plan of dated deliverables, named completion evidence and an interim control.

checklist.step: Fix the illustration engine and system defects
actions: Raise the change request against the illustration engine or policy administration configuration citing the finding number, and specify the rule to be enforced — mandatory signature capture, state narrative selection by group situs, blocked illustration on non-illustrated plan codes, scale ceiling at the disciplined current scale.
Have the QA Analyst build test cases from the examiner's own failing records so the fix is proven against the actual defect.
Run the change through the normal release path with regression on the illustration output format, and record the release id and production date.
Confirm post-release that a previously failing scenario now blocks or warns as designed, and attach the evidence to the tracker record.
checklist.done: the configuration change is released with test cases built from the examiner's failing records and post-release proof attached.

checklist.step: Amend the illustration procedure and re-issue it
actions: Redline the Life Insurance Illustration Compliance Procedure section the finding exposed, naming the finding number in the version history.
Where the finding arose in one state but the practice is used in the other 44, amend the base procedure rather than adding a single state exception.
Route the redline through Regulatory Counsel and the illustration actuary and obtain Head of Compliance approval out of the normal annual cycle.
Publish with a read-and-attest task to every affected role and a 15-business-day due date.
checklist.done: the amended procedure is approved, published out of cycle and attested by every affected role.

checklist.step: Retrain and sanction the producers behind the finding
actions: Identify every producer whose business appears in the finding population, not just those in the examiner's sample.
Assign the targeted illustration module with a 30-day completion window and a required pass mark, and track completion by producer number.

Apply the consequence-ladder step the procedure specifies for the behaviour found — coaching, suspension of new business authority, or termination review — and record the step and its date in the producer record.
Report completion and sanction status to the Compliance Manager for the finding's closure pack.
checklist.done: every producer in the finding population has a completed targeted module or a recorded sanction with a date.

checklist.step: Compute and pay policyholder restitution where the finding requires it
actions: Where the finding is that certificates were sold on a non-conforming or unsupportable illustration, agree the restitution methodology with Regulatory Counsel and the state before any payment is made.
Build the restitution register: certificate number, state, owner, the illustrated versus actual values, the shortfall, interest at the state's required rate, and the payment amount.
Have the Actuary review the shortfall calculation on a 25-record sample before the run and sign the methodology.
Execute payments through the policy administration system with a distinct transaction code, and send the state-approved policyholder letter with each payment.
Reconcile payments made to the register and report the completion rate to the examiner-in-charge.
checklist.done: a signed-off restitution register is fully paid, reconciled and reported to the examiner with the approved letter issued to each owner.

checklist.step: Run the read-across to the other Model 582 jurisdictions
actions: Take the finding's root cause and test whether the same defect exists in each of the other 44 jurisdictions using the state-split population.
Where the defect exists, extend the corrective action and, where the state's regulation requires it, assess whether a voluntary self-report is warranted with Regulatory Counsel.
Where the defect does not exist, record why — different state narrative, different plan codes sold, different producer set — rather than leaving the state blank.
Report the read-across result to the compliance committee alongside the finding itself.
checklist.done: every one of the other 44 jurisdictions is marked affected or not affected with a written reason, and self-report decisions are recorded.

checklist.step: Re-test each corrective action before claiming completion
actions: For each completed action, draw a fresh sample of 25 records created after the fix date and test the specific defect the finding described.
Test the interim control's operation for the period between the response date and the fix date, since the examiner will ask what protected policyholders in the gap.
Record the re-test result, sample size and date on the tracker record and mark the action complete only on a clean result.
Where the re-test fails, reopen the action with a new date and notify the Head of Compliance the same day.
checklist.done: each action is marked complete only on a clean 25-record post-fix re-test with the interim control's operation also evidenced.

checklist.step: Report remediation status to the examiner and to the committee until closure
actions: Send the examiner-in-charge a status report at each committed milestone stating actions complete, actions in flight and any date at risk, before the date slips rather than after.
Table the same status at the compliance committee each month while findings remain open, with the ageing of every overdue action.
Escalate any action more than 30 days past its committed date to the board risk committee with the reason and a recovery date.
Where a regulatory settlement agreement or consent order sets terms, track those terms as findings in their own right until each is satisfied.
checklist.done: the examiner and the committee both hold a current status at every milestone and every overdue action is escalated.

checklist.step: Assemble the closure pack per finding and obtain sign-off
actions: Assemble per finding: finding text, response, root cause, corrective action plan, implementation evidence (release ids, procedure version, training completion, restitution register), re-test results and the read-across record.
Route to the Head of Compliance for closure sign-off, with Regulatory Counsel confirming nothing remains that requires disclosure to the state.
File the pack in the compliance evidence repository under REG-012-C05 and the exam reference, with the 7-year retention label from the closing letter date.
Link the pack into the market conduct exam readiness file's prior-findings section so the next examiner finds it without asking.
checklist.done: each finding has a signed closure pack filed under the exam reference and linked into the exam readiness file.

checklist.step: Keep the corrective control alive after the state closes the exam
actions: Convert every corrective action that created an ongoing control into a scheduled control on the GRC platform with an owner, a frequency and a required evidence type.
Add each converted control to the quarterly conduct monitoring scorecard so a lapse shows up as a metric, not only at the next exam.
Schedule a 12-month sustainability re-test per finding and diary it against the control record.
Record the closing letter date and the finding reference on the control so a repeat finding can be traced to its origin.
checklist.done: every ongoing corrective control is scheduled, monitored on the scorecard and diarised for a 12-month sustainability re-test.

testing.step: Build the population of illustration-related market conduct findings
actions: Extract every finding record in the tracker relating to Group Life illustrations, with citing state, receipt date, response due date, corrective actions, committed dates and status.
Add findings from any draft or final examination report received in the period that has no tracker record, since an unlogged finding is the worst case.
Reconcile the tracker population to the final examination reports filed in the exam readiness file and resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the finding population is reconciled to the filed examination reports and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile each finding to the examiner's own report text
actions: Open the final examination report and compare the finding text, the cited standard and the examiner's error rate to the tracker record.
Flag any tracker record whose wording narrows the finding relative to the report — a narrowed finding produces a narrowed fix.
Confirm every finding in the report has exactly one tracker record and no finding was merged away.
List discrepancies as exceptions before any sampling judgement is made.
testing.done: every tracker record is reconciled word-for-word to the report finding with narrowed or merged findings listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample of findings, certificates and payments
actions: Take 100% of findings involving restitution, self-report decisions or a regulatory settlement agreement, and 100% of findings closed late.
Take 5 further findings at random on a recorded seed, for a minimum of 10 findings.
For each sampled finding, draw 25 post-fix certificates and, where restitution ran, 25 payment records.
Record the seed, population sizes and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all restitution, self-report and late findings plus a reproducible random draw with per-finding record samples.

testing.step: Recompute the response and milestone deadline maths
actions: For each sampled finding, take the draft report receipt date and the state's stated response window and recompute the response due date.
Compare it to the transmission confirmation date of the company's response and state days late where it is late.
Recompute each corrective action's days late as actual completion date minus committed date, using an examiner-granted extension only where written evidence exists.
Confirm the day 7, 15 and 25 alerts fired and were closed by a named person during the response window.
testing.done: response and milestone dates are recomputed with days late stated and alert operation confirmed.

testing.step: Challenge the root cause and the exposure period independently
actions: Read the finding and form your own view of the root cause before opening the company's analysis.
Test the stated exposure period against the change history of the illustration engine, the procedure version history and the training records.
Where the company's exposure period is shorter than the evidence supports, the affected population was undersized and every downstream action is understated — record this as a significant exception.
Capture the change and version histories relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled finding has an independent root cause view and a tested exposure period with undersized populations flagged.

testing.step: Re-perform the post-fix test on fresh records
actions: For each sampled finding, pull the 25 post-fix certificates and test the exact defect the examiner described — missing signature, non-conforming content, wrong state narrative, illustration produced on a non-illustrated plan.
Confirm the illustration engine release the company cited is actually in production and applies to the plan codes in scope.
Compare your defect rate to the company's re-test result; a clean company re-test alongside a failing independent re-test is a closure-integrity exception.
Capture the failing records and the release evidence into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled finding has an independent post-fix defect rate compared to the company's re-test result.

testing.step: Recompute restitution amounts and trace the payments
actions: Recompute the shortfall for 25 sampled restitution records on the agreed methodology, including interest at the state's required rate and the correct period.
Trace each recomputed amount to the payment transaction in the policy administration system, matching the distinct restitution transaction code, the amount and the value date.
Confirm the state-approved policyholder letter was issued with each payment and that unclaimed or returned payments were followed up rather than written back.
Any shortfall against the recomputed amount, or any register row with no payment, is a fail.
testing.done: sampled restitution is recomputed, traced to a coded payment and matched to an issued policyholder letter.

testing.step: Test the read-across across the other 44 jurisdictions
actions: For each sampled finding, read the read-across record and confirm every one of the other 44 jurisdictions is marked affected or not affected with a written reason.
Independently test 5 states marked not affected by pulling 10 certificates each and testing the same defect.
Confirm any self-report decision was made with Regulatory Counsel and is documented with its rationale and date.
A state marked not affected where the defect is present is a significant exception with disclosure implications.
testing.done: the read-across is complete for all 44 other jurisdictions and 5 not-affected states are independently retested.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the finding, the state, what failed — late response, undersized population, failed post-fix re-test, restitution shortfall, incomplete read-across — and the regulatory exposure.
Assign a root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date inside 30 days for anything the examiner could still test.
Where a closed finding is shown not to be remediated, reopen it, notify the Head of Compliance the same day and assess with Regulatory Counsel whether the state must be told.
Carry every open exception into the next finding-closure test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, with falsely closed findings reopened and assessed for disclosure.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the remediation test
actions: Compute the on-time closure rate against committed dates, the independent post-fix defect rate and the restitution accuracy rate, and compare each to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who designed and signed off none of the sampled corrective actions, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any falsely closed finding and any disclosure decision to the compliance committee and the board risk committee, and file the workpaper under REG-012-C05.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with closure rate, post-fix defect rate, restitution accuracy, stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed.
